title: Bhishma Parva (the Gita re-read in place, 6 sessions)
hook: Krishna says he taught this teaching to the sun long ago, and Arjuna, his cousin, objects: you were born after the sun.
carry: better your own duty, done imperfectly
tomorrow: Bhishma Parva (the Gita re-read in place, 6 sessions)

segments.voice: Yesterday in the Bhishma Parva, Arjuna said: I am your disciple, teach me. And Krishna, as if smiling, began. Whom did you ask to teach you something? Day eight hundred twenty-two.

Families have a way of keeping each other honest. Tell a story about yourself at a holiday dinner, and someone who grew up with you will say: that's not how it happened. Something like that happens in the middle of the Gita. Krishna mentions, almost in passing, that he taught this same teaching long ago, to the sun. And Arjuna, his cousin, stops him. Wait. Your birth came later. The sun was born long before you. How could you have taught him? Session four of six: the argument in the chariot.
screen: `FAMILY KEEPS YOU HONEST` → `I TAUGHT THIS TO THE SUN` → `WAIT: YOU WERE BORN AFTER HIM`

segments.voice: Read in place, Arjuna is not a polite student. He pushes back like a soldier who needs an answer before the fighting starts. At the start of the third chapter he says, more or less: if you think understanding is better than action, why are you pushing me into this terrible action? You're confusing me. Tell me one thing for certain. Krishna doesn't tell him to go and think in a cave. He says no one can stay free of action, even for a moment. Your nature moves you whether you like it or not. So act, but don't act for the prize. Act as an offering. He points to King Janaka, who reached the goal through action. He points to himself: there's nothing I need, he says, and yet I keep working, because the world follows what the great ones do. Then a line that cuts close for Arjuna: better your own duty, done imperfectly, than someone else's done well. Arjuna's duty, as a warrior, is standing across the field from him. Then the fourth chapter, and the moment from the hook. When Arjuna objects that Krishna was born after the sun, Krishna doesn't laugh it off. He says many births have passed for both of them. I know them all, he says, and you don't. Whenever dharma fails and its opposite rises, I come into being, age after age, to protect the good and set dharma right. This is where the cousin in the driver's seat begins to show Arjuna who he is. And it happens because Arjuna argued.
screen: `WHY PUSH ME INTO THIS ACTION?` · `NO ONE CAN STAY FREE OF ACTION` · `BETTER YOUR OWN DUTY, IMPERFECT` · then, large: `I KNOW MY BIRTHS. YOU DON'T.`

segments.voice: Sit and let your hands rest open in your lap. Think of one task waiting for you today, a small, ordinary one. Breathing in, see yourself doing it. Breathing out, let go of how it will turn out: the praise, the result, whether anyone notices. Do this a few times, the task in, the outcome out. That's the shape of what Krishna told Arjuna: act fully, and loosen your grip on the prize. If you pray, you can offer that task in your prayer. The bell holds the time.
Bhishma Parva. The book where a soldier argues with his teacher in the middle of a battlefield, and the argument opens the door.
Your line: better your own duty, done imperfectly. Today, do one task well, and don't check how it was received. Day eight hundred twenty-two.

howItsDone: The Gita's third and fourth chapters, on action without attachment and on Krishna's coming age after age, are read and recited both on their own and as part of the Bhishma Parva.

match.prompt: who said what in the chariot? tap the pairs.
pairs: why push me into this terrible action?
no one stays free of action

myth: Krishna told Arjuna to give up action and retreat to think

Arjuna objected that Krishna was born after the sun
and Krishna answered that many births had passed for both of them.
Krishna said another's duty done well is better than your own done badly
he said the reverse: better your own duty, even done imperfectly.

fork.setup: you're Arjuna. your cousin says he taught this teaching to the sun long ago. you know when he was born. what do you say?
options: but you were born after the sun. how can that be?
you're joking. let's get back to the battle.
fork.reveal: Arjuna objects, and Krishna answers: many births have passed for both of us; I know them all, and you don't.

original.note: dharma: what Krishna says he comes to set right, age after age, whenever it fails.

trapdoor: what you thought: Arjuna listened quietly while Krishna taught.
what it means: in place, Arjuna argues: why push me to act, and how could you have taught the sun?
what a scholar hears: Krishna's words about coming age after age answer a cousin's objection, not an abstract question.

sources.work: Bhagavad Gita, within the Mahabharata's Bhishma Parva

sources.ref: Bhagavad Gita 4.1–4.8, the teaching given to Vivasvat (the sun); Arjuna's objection; many births; age after age

notes: All paraphrase. Confirm: 3.1–3.2 (why engage me in this terrible deed; you confuse me; tell me one thing for certain), 3.5 (no one can remain even a moment without action), 3.9 (action as sacrifice/offering), 3.20 (Janaka and others attained perfection by action), 3.21–3.22 (people follow the great; nothing I need, yet I act), 3.35, 4.1 (Vivasvat), 4.4 (Arjuna's objection), 4.5, 4.7–4.8.
Vivasvat is glossed as 'the sun'; confirm the Keeper is happy with that simplification.
The hook's holiday-dinner image is a modern framing, not in the text.

Editor pass: cut the unsupported claim that Arjuna had known Krishna all his life (and 'since childhood' in the fork); 'born recently' now follows 4.4 ('your birth came later'); fixed the match pair that made the sun the teacher instead of the one taught.
Audit (fresh pass): checked 3.1-4.8 paraphrases; no changes needed.
